content.title: 3 Million Bottles of Eye Drops Sold at Walgreens, Kroger and More Recalled, FDA Says
content.text: More than three million bottles of eye drops have been recalled due to “lack of assurance of sterility,” according to the Food and Drug Administration.The FDA initiated the recall on March 3.K.C. Pharmaceuticals, Inc., a company based in Pomona, California, manufactured the drops, which were sold under a variety of brand names. A total of eight products are part of the recall and can be purchased at a variety of retail outlets, including Walgreens, CVS, Rite Aid, Harris Teeter, Kroger, Publix, Good Neighbor Pharmacy, Good Sense and Meijer.1,023,096 bottles of Dry Eye Relief Drops589,848 bottles of Artificial Tears Sterile Lubricant Eye Drops378,144 bottles of Sterile Eye Drops Original Formula315,144 bottles of Sterile Eye Drops Redness Lubricant303,216 bottles of Eye Drops (advanced relief)245,184 bottles of Ultra Lubricating Eye Drops182, 484 bottles of Sterile Eye Drops AC74,016 bottles of Sterile Eye Drops Soothing TearsThe FDA has classified this as a Class II recall, which is “a situation in which use of or exposure to a violative product may cause temporary or medically reversible adverse health consequences or where the probability of serious adverse health consequences is remote.”In 2025, pharmaceutical manufacturer AvKare recalled more than 75,000 cases of eye drops following an FDA audit that found manufacturing deviations during production.
